extracted.intended_audience: Harvard community (students, faculty, administrators) and general readers concerned with academic integrity and campus governance
extracted.subtask_description: An editorial arguing that a prominent figure accused of plagiarism should resign and face institutional consequences; it cites Harvard student handbook rules and discusses how intent, negligence, and extent of unattributed material affect appropriate responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish own ideas from sourced information (FAS Handbook guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Students should always take great care to distinguish their own ideas and knowledge from information derived from sources…Whenever ideas or facts are derived from a student’s reading and research or from a student’s own writings, the sources must be indicated…"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted from the Faculty of Arts and Sciences Handbook for Students: students are required to mark clearly what is theirs vs. what is derived from sources; failing to do so is a breach of academic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary consequence for uncredited student work
rubrics_metrics.description: "Students who, for whatever reason, submit work either not their own or without clear attribution to its sources will be subject to disciplinary action, and ordinarily required to withdraw from the College."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handbook prescribes disciplinary action up to (and ordinarily including) mandatory withdrawal for students whose work is uncredited or not their own — a formal institutional penalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation must report academic-dishonesty withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any letter of recommendation written for you on behalf of Harvard College — including letters to graduate schools, law schools, and medical schools — will report that you were required to withdraw for academic dishonesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical consequence: a required withdrawal for dishonesty is recorded in official recommendations, affecting students' future career/education opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leaders/Overseers must model academic integrity and may need to resign
rubrics_metrics.description: As an Overseer, Goodwin is a leader of an academic community, the foundation of which is integrity in independent scholarship. As a leader, she should recognize that her action is unbecoming an Overseer and resign her post immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial stance: individuals in governance or high-profile academic roles are held to standards of scholarly integrity; plagiarism by such figures undermines their legitimacy and may warrant resignation to preserve institutional credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent and pattern of unattributed use determines severity
rubrics_metrics.description: The unattributed use of sources goes far beyond borrowing isolated phrases...but rather involved many more uncited works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece distinguishes isolated accidental phrasing from systematic unattributed use; broader, repeated uncited borrowing increases the seriousness of the offense and the appropriate institutional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentional plagiarism via gross negligence is unacceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though the plagiarism was apparently unintentional, Goodwin’s gross negligence—losing primary works, not checking citations before publication—constitutes the lack of respect and appreciation of others’ work that cannot be condoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intent does not fully excuse plagiarism: carelessness such as failing to track sources or verify citations is treated as serious misconduct because it shows disrespect for others' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoring credibility requires concrete consequences and steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Goodwin has a long road ahead of her before she restores her credibility as an historian or journalist—the NewsHour...has already announced that she will be taking a leave from the show...The first step should be resigning from the University’s oldest governing board...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To repair reputation after plagiarism, the editorial recommends tangible actions (leaves of absence, resignations) so the individual and the institution demonstrate accountability and protect collective reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolated accidental citation errors may warrant different response
rubrics_metrics.description: If this were one accidental case of incorrect citation, the situation may warrant a different response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece concedes that context matters: a single accidental citation error could be handled differently from repeated or extensive unattributed borrowing, implying proportionality in sanctions.
